events.title: The agent looks for patterns in its weak turns
events.detail: Once the past week has at least five low-scoring turns, it clusters them and drafts edits to its own prompt. Nothing lands until I reply on Telegram with a command like `apply 1 2`, and until the judge passes a calibration check it only reports the clusters.

events.title: An LLM judge scores the day's conversations
events.detail: It pulls up to 25 of the past day's conversation traces from Langfuse and scores each on task completion, tool-call efficiency, and response quality. Checked against a stronger model's labels, it hasn't cleared the bar for trust, so its scores sort what I look at; they don't decide anything.

events.title: Backups snapshot, then sync
events.detail: The SQLite databases get an atomic snapshot instead of a raw file copy, then sync to two drives: an SD card for a full rebuild, and a USB drive with the critical data that my Mac can read if the Pi dies. Each run reports its own result, so a failed backup shows up the same day.

events.title: The Pi's config gets copied off the box
events.detail: The Mac pulls the Pi's service definitions into a private Git repo. It copies an explicit list of files instead of excluding the risky ones, so a credential a service drops next to its config never gets swept in.

events.title: The agent writes my morning brief
events.detail: A script collects the Pi's health and my calendar first, so those facts come from the systems instead of the model. Then the agent searches the web through a search engine on the Pi and sends one Telegram message: system status, today's schedule, tech news, and things to do in NYC.

events.title: New llama.cpp commits get flagged before a rebuild
events.detail: A script compares the running build with upstream and lists the new commits that touch this AMD GPU path or the features the model relies on. Upstream moves fast enough to break this hardware, so I read those before deciding to rebuild.
